results.title: 计算机视觉与模式识别2025_7_29
results.content: **摘要**：大型视觉语言模型（LVLM）具有先进的多模态学习，但由于大量的视觉标记而面临高计算成本，从而激励标记修剪以提高推理效率。关键的挑战在于确定哪些令牌真正重要。大多数现有的方法依赖于基于注意力的标准来估计令牌的重要性。然而，它们固有地受到某些限制，例如位置偏见。在这项工作中，我们探索了一个新的角度令牌的重要性的基础上令牌过渡LVLM。我们观察到，令牌表示的过渡提供了一个有意义的信号的语义信息。基于这一认识，我们提出了一种无需训练且高效的令牌修剪方法TransPrune。具体来说，TransPrune通过组合令牌转换变化（TTV）（测量令牌表示的幅度和方向的变化）和指令引导注意力（IGA）（测量指令通过注意力关注图像令牌的强度）来评估其重要性，从而逐步修剪令牌。大量的实验表明，TransPrune在八个基准测试中实现了与原始LVLM（如LLaVA-v1.5和LLaVA-Next）相当的多模态性能，同时将推理TFLOPs减少了一半以上。此外，TTV本身可以作为一个有效的标准，而不依赖于注意力，实现性能与基于注意力的方法。该守则将在接受该文件后在https: github.com liaolea TransPrune上公布。**摘要**：Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have advanced multimodal learning but face high computational costs due to the large number of visual tokens, motivating token pruning to improve inference efficiency. **摘要**：文本到图像（T2 I）生成模型已经彻底改变了内容创建，但仍然对提示措辞高度敏感，通常需要用户多次重复优化提示，而没有明确的反馈。虽然自动提示工程、受控文本嵌入、去噪和多回合生成等技术可以缓解这些问题，但它们提供的可控性有限，或者通常需要额外的训练，从而限制了泛化能力。因此，我们引入了T2 I-Copilot，这是一个无需训练的多智能体系统，它利用（多模态）大型语言模型之间的协作来自动化提示短语，模型选择和迭代优化。与直接生成相比，这种方法显著简化了即时工程，同时提高了生成质量和文本图像对齐。具体来说，T2 I-Copilot由三个代理组成：（1）输入解释器，它解析输入提示，解决歧义，并生成一个标准化的报告;（2）生成引擎，它从不同类型的T2 I模型中选择合适的模型，并组织视觉和文本提示，以启动生成;和（3）质量评估器，其评估美学质量和文本图像对齐，提供分数和潜在再生的反馈。T2 I-Copilot可以完全自主操作，同时还支持人为干预，以实现精细控制。在GenAI-Bench上，使用开源生成模型，T2 I-Copilot实现了与商业模型RecraftV 3和Imagen 3相当的VQA得分，仅以16.59%的成本超过FLUX1.1-pro 6.17%，并超过FLUX.1-dev和SD 3.5 Large 9.11%和6.36%。代码将在https: github.com SHI-Labs T2I-Copilot上发布。**摘要**：Text-to-Image (T2I) generative models have revolutionized content creation but remain highly sensitive to prompt phrasing, often requiring users to repeatedly refine prompts multiple times without clear feedback. Thus, we introduce T2I-Copilot, a training-free multi-agent system that leverages collaboration between (Multimodal) Large Language Models to automate prompt phrasing, model selection, and iterative refinement. Specifically, T2I-Copilot consists of three agents: (1) Input Interpreter, which parses the input prompt, resolves ambiguities, and generates a standardized report; (2) Generation Engine, which selects the appropriate model from different types of T2I models and organizes visual and textual prompts to initiate generation; and (3) Quality Evaluator, which assesses aesthetic quality and text-image alignment, providing scores and feedback for potential regeneration.

results.title: Track: Poster Session 1
results.content: The density of states (DOS) is a spectral property of crystalline materials, which provides fundamental insights into various characteristics of the materials.While previous works mainly focus on obtaining high-quality representations of crystalline materials for DOS prediction, we focus on predicting the DOS from the obtained representations by reflecting the nature of DOS: DOS determines the general distribution of states as a function of energy.That is, DOS is not solely determined by the crystalline material but also by the energy levels, which has been neglected in previous works.In this paper, we propose to integrate heterogeneous information obtained from the crystalline materials and the energies via a multi-modal transformer, thereby modeling the complex relationships between the atoms in the crystalline materials and various energy levels for DOS prediction.Moreover, we propose to utilize prompts to guide the model to learn the crystal structural system-specific interactions between crystalline materials and energies.Extensive experiments on two types of DOS, i.e., Phonon DOS and Electron DOS, with various real-world scenarios demonstrate the superiority of DOSTransformer.The source code for DOSTransformer is available at https://github.com/HeewoongNoh/DOSTransformer.
